title: When one parent is enough
question: How can a plant reproduce with only one parent, and what does that cost?
hook: A clipping from a spider plant can grow into a whole new plant with no partner needed.
idea: Asexual reproduction makes clones of a single parent, while sexual reproduction mixes gametes into genetically different offspring.

beats.prompt: You root a cutting from a spider plant. How will the new plant compare with its parent?

choices.label: It will be genetically identical to the parent
It will be a mix of the parent and a second plant
choices.feedback: Mixing happens when gametes fuse, but a cutting involves only one parent and no gamete fusion.

choices.label: It will differ from the parent in many traits
choices.feedback: Different offspring come from sexual reproduction; a cutting is a clone of its one parent.

beats.explain: A cutting produces a new individual without gametes fusing, so it is a clone, genetically identical to the parent.

beats.prompt: match each plant to the part it uses to reproduce vegetatively
beats.explain: Each of these plants makes new individuals from a modified underground or trailing part of the parent.

beats.prompt: sort each statement into the kind of reproduction it describes
items: Offspring differ genetically from either parent
Gametes fuse to make the offspring
Male and female gametes are not made and joined
beats.explain: Sexual reproduction fuses gametes and gives different offspring; asexual reproduction uses one parent and passes its characteristics on.

beats.prompt: one step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A gardener roots cuttings from one prized plant.
A cutting is vegetative reproduction, so no gametes fuse.
So each new plant will differ genetically from the parent.
If the parent carried a disease, the new plants may inherit it.
beats.explain: With no gametes fusing, the new plants are clones, genetically identical to the parent, which is also why a disease can pass on.
